# Grid cell editing still speaks the pre-View-anchor focus dialect — keyboard mount dead, editors abandoned as zombies

## The defect

`grid.View` centralizes DOM focus by design: the View element is the single logical focus anchor (`tabIndex: '-1'`), cells never take DOM focus, and the View's own doc block says the keyboard half of that centralization "left keyboard migration for follow-up". `table.plugin.CellEditing` — which `grid.plugin.CellEditing` inherits nearly verbatim — was never migrated. Four paths break, all witnessed live on a consumer grid (source-provable on current `dev`; no console error surfaces on any of them):

1. **Enter/Space can never mount an editor.** The plugin registers its keys on `owner.body.keys` (CellEditing.mjs `construct`), but with the View holding DOM focus, keydowns target the View element — the body subtree never contains the focused node, so those handlers are unreachable. A consumer independently documented this in its own source ("Enter/Space, registered on `owner.body.keys`, do nothing in this version") and registered its F2 on `view.keys` as the workaround.
2. **The guard is dead even if the keys moved.** `onTableKeyDown` reads `data.target.cls?.includes('neo-selected')` — the key target is the View under the anchor model, never the selected cell. The selected cell must come from the `selectionModel`, not from the event target.
3. **`focusCells` is a silent no-op.** `selectCell` ends with `me.owner.focus(cellId)`; `DomAccess.focus` on a non-focusable node without `children: true` does nothing, and cells are deliberately not focusable. Measured: after every editor gesture, `document.activeElement` is the View, never a cell — so cell-level focusEnter/focusLeave can never fire, which is exactly how the defect presents to a consumer.
4. **Abandoned editors become zombies.** Clicking another cell in the same grid moves focus input→View — inside the owner, so the plugin's `focusLeave` (container-level) correctly never fires, and the mounted editor just stays in the old cell. Re-triggering an edit on that cell then runs `mountEditor`'s unmount-stale-editor branch and ends with `editor.focus()` — measured result: the editor is re-mounted in the DOM but `activeElement` stays the View; the field renders and typing goes nowhere. The `onSelectionChange` hook that should own the cell-switch story is a stubbed TODO.

Implementation surfaced three more, all witnessed:

5. **`mountEditor` can never resolve a grid cell.** It calls `body.getCellId(record, dataField)`, but the grid signature is `(rowIndex, dataField)` — a record argument turns the pooled row id into `…__row-NaN`, the vdom lookup returns nothing, and the mount dies as a silent unhandled rejection. A consumer independently shimmed exactly this (a body subclass accepting both forms) — stock `cellEditing: true` on a grid has never mounted an editor.
6. **The unmount suspicion is confirmed, and worse.** `unmountEditor` runs `body.getVdomRoot().cn[rowIndex] = body.createRow(...)` — `createRow` does not exist on `grid.Body` (rows are pooled components), so EVERY unmount path throws in the worker: the stale-editor branch (the zombie) and the `focusLeave` handler itself. "focusLeave not working" is literal — it fires and its handler crashes.
7. **The plugin connects to the wrong selection-model host.** It reads and listens on `owner.selectionModel` / owner's `selectionModelChange`, but grids host the model on the VIEW (`grid.Container.view.selectionModel` — the engine's own example reads it there). On a grid the plugin's model wiring never connected at all.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Enter/Space on a grid with a selected cell mounts the editor for that cell: keys live on the View's registry (the documented single key registry), and the target cell comes from the selection model. Headless spec: select → Enter → the editor input holds DOM focus.
- [ ] `focusCells` either performs a real focus (View-anchored, per the design comment) or retires; no silent no-op call path remains.
- [ ] Switching the selected cell while an editor is mounted settles the editor (submit-or-unmount — pick and document the polarity) instead of abandoning it; the `onSelectionChange` TODO resolves or is removed with its reason.
- [ ] Re-invoking edit on a cell that carries a stale editor produces a mounted AND focused editor (spec pins `document.activeElement` = the editor input after the second invocation).
- [ ] Container-level `focusLeave` keeps unmounting the editor when DOM focus truly leaves the grid (existing behavior pinned so the migration cannot regress it).
- [ ] Grid cell resolution works for record inputs (the pooled-row index derivation lives in the grid plugin), and the unmount path redraws pooled rows via the row component — no `createRow` call against `grid.Body` remains.
- [ ] The selection model resolves from its actual host (view where present, owner otherwise) for connect, key-path resolution, and settle.

## Origin

Consumer-workspace triage (agent session 914dffcd-0057-46a5-a0c6-9ca807fd5c91): an editable grid where keyboard editing never worked and a once-abandoned editor could not be re-entered. Related: the grid multi-body/View focus centralization (grid/View.mjs doc block), `table.plugin.CellEditing` (the shared implementation), `examples/grid/cellEditing` (same dialect, same exposure).

Closing as superseded by the live architecture authority: [D#17832](https://github.com/orgs/neomjs/discussions/17832) owns grid cell editing end to end — its Author's Note carries the operator's pre-publication boundary (an independent Grid implementation, never a Table-plugin extension), which this ticket's implementation path violated. PR #17937 was dropped on that ground with the diagnosis preserved.

What this ticket contributes to the successor (pinned in the D#17832 salvage): the seven witnessed defects (the discussion had already measured the silent mount failure; the unmount-path worker crash — which is what made `focusLeave` appear dead — the selection-model host mismatch, and the pooled-row redraw idiom appear additive), the real-browser component fixture with real-keydown arms, and the two named spec gaps (invalid-editor terminal, Table control).

No successor implementation ticket before D#17832 graduates — the epic and its slices are the landing pad.
